question: Can a cached stronger L/14 teacher improve unseen-product retrieval when the B/16 final block can adapt, without increasing serving encoder or gallery footprint?
population: official SOP TRAIN 59,551 images; seed-179019 53,700 fit images in 10,186 products and 5,851 heldout images in 1,132 disjoint products; no official test image bytes
input_view: canonical authenticated UNICOM B/16 image view, cached as exact float32 input to its final transformer block; no random image augmentation in this screen
controls: all arms start from the same authenticated pretrained B/16, fit-only PCA-initialized 768-to-128 compact head and fit-only normalized class-centroid proxies; tail arms alone update final transformer block; teacher arms alone add cached L/14 row-relation KL
schedule: NumPy PCG64 seed179019, five full product-coverage passes; 32 distinct products per batch, two distinct images per product, 1,595 identical 64-image updates per trained arm; final checkpoint only
optimizer: AdamW with zero weight decay; LR final block 1e-5, compact head 1e-4, class proxies 1e-3; global trainable-gradient norm clip 1
loss: ArcFace margin0.3 scale64 on normalized 128-D compact features in all arms; teacher arms add coefficient1.0 rowwise KL(teacher||student) over off-diagonal pair scores at temperature0.1, using normalized 768-D cached L/14 teacher cosine and Sfora's exact-forward 130-byte signed-int8/f16 packed-score straight-through surrogate

advance_gate: tail_teacher gains at least +1.0 percentage point holdout-only packed Recall@1 over each of head_teacher and tail_arcface, with each paired 1,132-product bootstrap 95% lower bound above zero; no point regression against tail_arcface in full-TRAIN-gallery Recall@1 or holdout-only mAP@R; otherwise kill this partial-tail teacher recipe
